content: Could there be a linter checking that all new instances cannot already be inferred (ie instance : Foo := bar should complain if instance : Foo := inferInstance succeeds in the same place)? This would have prevented the issue in #AI authored projects > Comparator-related import subtleties

Note that there are many instances in mathlib which can be inferred already and are added for shortcut or decidability reasons. However in almost all of these cases the proof is by infer_instance or inferInstance (we seem to use both) so any such linter would probably have to not flag these proofs.
Or adding set_option ... false in before such declaration also signals that they are intended exceptions to the linter.
The instance diamond linter that I'm working on will at least verify that the two different instances are defeq to eachother.
But I think the linter you are asking for needs to run at the place where the instance is declared, rather than while importing all of mathlib like the instance diamond linter.
Yes, exactly. That's what I tried to communicate above

Thinking about it again, I believe a better linter would be to warn when using inferInstanceAs Foo when the expected type Bar is instance-reducibly the same as Foo. It should generate Try this: inferInstance.
In that case, it needs to be implemented by core
And this linter could clearly not be mathlib-specific.
Why "needs"? Can't we override the inferInstanceAs notation in/before Mathlib.Init?
Well yes that's true, but it would be a bit annoying.
